newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev dips at close, seen rising on IMF deal.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev dips at close, seen rising on IMF deal.

text.p: The lev closed at 1,498-1,508 per dollar, off midday highs of 1,480-1,500 but up from the previous close of 1,525-1,530 following approval of a credit package by the International Monetary Fund, dealers said.
"Dollar demand from clients briefly rose in the afternoon, pushing the lev down from midday highs. But the lev retained most of early gains by the close as dollar demand waned," one dealer said.
Dealers expected the lev to continue its advance tomorrow as dollar supply was likely to top demand on profit taking in favour of high-yield lev denominated investments.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was seen buying foreign currency today, containing the lev rise, traders said. BNB officials were not available for comment.

The lev gained to 1,480-1,500 to dollar at midday from the morning's 1,480-1,530 as dollar supply from clients rose on profit taking following approval of a $657 million credit package to Bulgaria by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The IMF board late on Friday approved a 14-month $509 million stand-by facility for Bulgaria to support the country's move towards market economy and additional $148 million to make up for a serious decline in its cereal yields. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
